notes.basket: The breakfast basket, an index averaging coffee, sugar, wheat, and orange juice prices normalized to 2015 as 100, currently stands at 132, indicating a roughly 32% increase since 2015. This rise is uneven across the components and has occurred in recent years rather than gradually. The index reflects changes in global commodity prices, which are sensitive to specific supply factors rather than general inflation trends. The basket provides a snapshot of cost pressures in common breakfast-related commodities.
notes.movers: The principal contributors to the basket's increase are coffee, which rose 93% since 2015, and orange juice, up 22%, while wheat and sugar showed more modest changes of 7% and 5%, respectively. These shifts are largely driven by supply disruptions related to weather events and crop diseases—such as frost and drought in arabica coffee regions and citrus greening coupled with hurricanes affecting orange juice production. These commodities trade in relatively thin markets, meaning that small changes in supply can lead to outsized price moves rather than broad economic inflation factors.
notes.why: Price movements in this basket are primarily governed by a few weather-exposed soft commodities prone to volatile conditions that influence global supply. Because these factors are structural rather than cyclical, elevated prices could persist over an extended period. Monitoring these specific agricultural risks provides insight into the drivers of commodity cost trends reflected in this index.
